page: Vultr vcg-a40-12c-60g-24vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud server designed for workloads requiring dedicated graphics processing capabilities alongside balanced compute resources. Positioned within the Cloud GPU family, this instance utilizes a fractional GPU allocation to deliver hardware-accelerated performance without the overhead of a full dedicated GPU.

The hardware configuration features 12 vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores of an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI). System memory totals 60.0 GB, providing 5.0 GB of RAM per core. Graphics acceleration is delivered by a fractional 0.5 NVIDIA A40 Ampere GPU, which provides 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1110 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this instance in the average tier across multiple performance metrics. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1631.08, while the multi-core score reaches 20624.31. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks show read speeds of 123.01 GB/sec and write speeds of 53.08 GB/sec. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the server achieves a prompt processing speed of 1048.4 tokens per second and a text generation speed of 219.1 tokens per second. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing drops to 23.45 tokens per second, while text generation averages 9.43 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the fractional GPU model allows users to access enterprise-grade NVIDIA Ampere architecture and 24 GB of VRAM at a lower resource density and cost compared to full GPU instances. However, the shared CPU allocation and 2.0 GHz clock speed present a tradeoff for CPU-bound tasks. This server is suitable for workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, data science jobs, machine learning model prototyping, and GPU-accelerated rendering or video processing.
